title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 118
paragraphs: Datis, meanwhile, as he was making his way to Asia with his army, saw a dream when he was at Myconos. The nature of the vision is not recorded, but as soon as day dawned he had the ships searched. In a Phoenician vessel he found an image of Apollo plated with gold, and he asked where it had been carried off from. When he was told the name of the temple, he sailed in his own ship to Delos, and finding the Delians now returned to the island, he deposited the statue in the temple and charged the Delians to convey it back to Delion in Theban territory, which lies on the seacoast just opposite Chalcis. Having given that order, Datis sailed away. The Delians, however, never returned the statue; it was the Thebans themselves who, twenty years later, brought it back to Delion, prompted by an oracle.
